      "name": "NumStability.IsQuasilinearConservationLawSolutionAt",
      "interpretation": "Existence of temporal and spatial state derivatives qt and qx satisfying qt + A(q(x,t))(qx) = 0 for the supplied continuous-linear-map field A.",
      "effect_on_target": "Every such predicate fails because its spatial derivative witness is impossible at the stipulated spatial discontinuity. No identification of A with the derivative of flux is needed for this negative conclusion.",

      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "NumStability.IsRectangleConservationLawSolution",
      "interpretation": "Every spatial state slice is integrable on every finite interval, every temporal endpoint-flux slice is likewise integrable, and the change in spatial mass between any two times equals the time integral of first-endpoint minus second-endpoint flux.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the conservation-solution premise. For fixed spatial endpoints, mass is an indefinite integral of a locally integrable flux difference plus a constant, yielding the asserted derivative almost everywhere.",

      "status": "pass"
    },
    {
